chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jaroud who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, and the thief does not steal while he is a believer, and the plunderer does not plunder a plunder of honor while he is a believer.'
Ibn Sinan said: I said to Abu al-Jaroud, 'And what is a plunder of honor?' He said, 'Similar to what Hatim did when he said, 'Whoever takes something, it is for him.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person's faith when they commit adultery or theft according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Khuruj min al-Iman' (exit from faith) during the commission of major sins, positing that faith and major sin are mutually exclusive in the moment of action. It specifically highlights 'plunder of honor' (nuhbat dhat sharaf) by citing Hatim al-Tai’s generosity, where taking an item was viewed as a gift rather than theft, illustrating how intent and social context affect the nature of the sin. This reflects the Mu'tazili-influenced view prevalent in al-Kafi that major sins remove one from the fold of Islam temporarily, distinct from the Ahl al-Sunnah view of 'faith with deficiency'.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘An adulterer would not commit adultery while he is a Believer, when he does commit adultery (he losses his faith at that very point),; and a thief does not steal when he does steal while he is a Believer; and a plunderer does not plunder with honour when he plunders it while he is a Believer’.
Ibn Sinan said, ‘I said to Abu Al-Jaroud, ‘And what is plundering with honour?’ He said, ‘Approximately what Hatim did when he said that anyone who takes something so it is for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from ‘Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa‘id who has said the following:

“Once, abu al-Hassan ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent one of the slaves to buy eggs for him. The slave took one or two eggs and gambled with them. When the slave came back he (the Imam) used the eggs for food. A servant told him (the Imam) about gambling. He (the Imam) asked for a washbowl and threw up.”
